ideal: A healthy repo shows it in Insights: every health file present, no finished branch left behind, and few runner minutes wasted.

parts.ideal: Work lands as small merged pull requests, few stay open, and issues close as fast as they open
parts.setup: Scored on the Pull requests, Issues and Code tabs; the code frequency API refuses a repo of 10,000 commits

parts.ideal: Every default-branch commit is credited to an account; a count of activity is no measure of a person
parts.setup: Link each commit email to an account; Claude Code contribution metrics credit agent work once turned on. Not scored: it rarely moves
Add a README, license, contributing guide, code of conduct, issue forms and a pull request template

parts.ideal: Not scored: no documented practice sets a goal for views, clones or forks
parts.setup: Traffic keeps 14 days and needs an admin token; its clones mostly count workflow checkouts

parts.ideal: Every manifest parses, so every dependency is known
parts.setup: Keep the graph on and commit lock files in a format it reads. Not scored: it rarely moves, and Security scores the alerts

parts.ideal: Only the default branch and live work remain; a leftover branch is gone within a day
parts.setup: Turn on automatic branch deletion; delete the branch of a pull request closed without merging; open a pull request within a day

parts.ideal: Everyone with write access has committed within 90 days
parts.setup: Review the people list each quarter and remove access nobody uses

parts.ideal: Under a tenth of billed minutes buys nothing; a check failing a pull request is not waste
parts.setup: GitHub offers no API for these two views; both are computed from workflow runs and jobs

quality: The health checklist is complete, no branch outlives its pull request, and access nobody uses is removed.
speed: A leftover branch is gone within a day of its pull request closing.
consumption: At most a tenth of billed runner minutes goes to runs that are cancelled, time out or fail after merge.
